rounds.text: Conceded: [E1], [E6], [E12], [E13], [E16], [E17], [E36], [E37], [E38], [E46], [E47], [E48], [E49]. Despite reported earnings growth, the company suffers from a severe cash flow crisis, bleeding ₹41 Cr in operating cash flow and ₹44 Cr in free cash flow as of March 2026 [E26, E27]. This translates to an alarming cash conversion ratio of -1.64x, where operating cash flow represents -82% of operating profit [E25, E28]. Concurrently, leverage is climbing rapidly as borrowings surged from ₹95 Cr to ₹155 Cr in a single year, pushing the debt-to-equity ratio to 1.48x and exceeding net worth [E29, E30]. Institutional confidence has evaporated entirely, marked by foreign institutions cutting stakes from 3.28% to 0.00% and domestic institutions reducing holdings from 1.89% to 0.11%, resulting in negative money flow [E33, E34, E35]. Compounded share price growth over the past year sits at a negative 2%, and the company pays a dividend yield of 0.00% despite reporting profits [E4, E18, E44]. Furthermore, high gold and silver prices have squeezed EBITDA margins down from 16% to 13%, with management explicitly flagging that price volatility and difficulties in passing costs to customers directly impact profit margins [E63, E69, E70].
